facts.text: Cale earned its name from early settler Cale Wardell, whose influence helped shape the town's early days.
Cale officially became an incorporated town on July 22, 1971, marking its formal recognition within Arkansas.
Cale sits on a 335‑foot ridge at 33°37′34″N 93°14′26″W, flanked by Little Caney Creek to the east and Big Caney Creek to the west.
Before the Civil War, federal land patents granted settlers such as Jessee C. and Capshaw, laying the groundwork for Cale's early farms.
After incorporation, Cale shifted from lumber to agriculture, cultivating cotton, corn, fruits, livestock, and poultry as its main economic drivers.
Barham Lake, a reservoir on Cale's north end, offers two connected lakes separated by a road and a public park on the south shore.
